MUSIC ACTIVITIES
 Week: Lesson:
 SCHOOL GRADE DATE TIME ROLL
 TWO
STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: LISTENING AND RESPONDING
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Elements of Music (listening and responding)
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:-
 a) Express initial personal reactions to musical performances for self-expression.
 b) Imitate short melodies with accuracy in pitch and rhythm for aural accuracy development.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
 a) How does the music make you feel?
 b) How should you feel when you hear this kind of music?
 c) How should you behave when listening to music?
 CORE COMPETENCIES VALUES PERTINENT CONTEMPORARY ISSUES
 (PCIs)
  Communication and  respect  life skills
 collaboration  Responsibility  decision making skills
  Creativity and imagination  unity  citizenship
  Digital literacy
  Self-efficacy
  Critical thinking
  Learning to learn
LEARNING RESOURCES:
  A repertoire of simple tunes.
  ICT devices such as mobile phones, laptops, tablets.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Group/individual work.
INTRODUCTION
Learners to sing a familiar song for warm up.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Learners to listen to live or recorded music.
 Step 2: Learners to tell what they can hear from the music
 Step 3: Conduct some simple vocal exercise. This can be achieved through “solfas” e.g
 dr:m.f:s.f:m.r:dd.m:s.d:s.m:d
 Step 4: Conduct aural dictations to individual and in groups. This can be done as a group competition
 SUMMARY
 Summarize the lesson by asking learners to describe their feeling after listening to a piece of music.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to sing simple melodies accurately in terms of pitch and rhythm.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
 Learners to practice at school and describe their feelings about the music they have listened.
REFLECTION ON THE LESSON/SELF-REMARKS
 MUSIC ACTIVITIES
 Week: Lesson:
 SCHOOL GRADE DATE TIME ROLL
 TWO
STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: LISTENING AND RESPONDING
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Performance Etiquette
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to respond to live or recorded performances with
appropriate audience behavior to enhance etiquette.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
 1) How do you feel when there is a lot of movement and noise during a musical performance?
 2) What is the importance of good behavior during a musical performance?
 3) As a music performer, how would you feel when there is a lot of interruption?
 CORE COMPETENCIES VALUES PERTINENT CONTEMPORARY ISSUES
 (PCIs)
  Communication and  respect  life skills
 collaboration  Responsibility  decision making skills
  Creativity and imagination  unity  citizenship
  Digital literacy
  Self-efficacy
  Critical thinking
  Learning to learn
LEARNING RESOURCES:
  ICT devises.
  Live/recorded music.
  Performance hall
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Group/individual work
INTRODUCTION
Arrange the hall appropriately for the performance.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Guide learners on appropriate behavior before and after performance.
 Step 2: Guide learners into watching a video clip of a performance with audience at the background.
 Step 3: Using questions guide learners on the dos and don’ts during performance.
 Step 4: Learners to appreciate music performance.
 SUMMARY:
 Performance can only be achieved through minimal interruption.
 CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
 Learners to adjudicate own performances.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Learners to observe appropriate behavior during school function perfomances.
REFLECTION ON THE LESSON/SELF-REMARKS

 Week: Lesson:
 SCHOOL GRADE DATE TIME ROLL
 TWO
STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: LISTENING AND RESPONDING
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Basic Music Terminology
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to use appropriate music terminology in
explaining/discussing music listened to for effective communication.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
Why is it important to use proper music terminology?
 CORE COMPETENCIES VALUES PERTINENT CONTEMPORARY ISSUES
 (PCIs)
  Communication and  respect  life skills
 collaboration  Responsibility  decision making skills
  Creativity and imagination  unity  citizenship
  Digital literacy
  Self-efficacy
  Critical thinking
  Learning to learn
LEARNING RESOURCES:
  ICT devises.
  List of music terminologies.
  Recorded/live music performance
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Group/individual
INTRODUCTION
Learners to sing a familiar song for warm up.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Learners to sing familiar and new songs and use them to discuss the various Music
 terminologies.
 Step 2: Learners to listen to and relate specific music to appropriate events such as national holidays.
 Step 3: Guide learners in discussing various elements of music i.e. loud, soft, fast, slow, high and low.
 Discuss their effects as well.
 Step 4: Learners to practice singing the songs in small groups.
 SUMMARY:
 Review the lesson and note summary points.
 CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to ask and answer questions.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Learners to prepare one or two songs to be presented in a community cultural festival or in a school
function.

 MUSIC ACTIVITIES
 Week: Lesson:
 SCHOOL GRADE DATE TIME ROLL
 One
STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: LISTENING AND RESPONDING
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Music Appreciation
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:-
 a) Appreciate and enjoy music drawn from diverse cultures and time through digital devices.
 b) Relate specific music to appropriate events in the community for effective communication.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
 1. What does the music that you hear make you think about?
 2. How does the music that you hear make you feel?
 CORE COMPETENCIES VALUES PERTINENT CONTEMPORARY ISSUES
 (PCIs)
  Communication and  respect  life skills
 collaboration  Responsibility  decision making skills
  Creativity and imagination  unity  citizenship
  Digital literacy
  Self-efficacy
  Critical thinking
  Learning to learn
LEARNING RESOURCES:
  ICT devises.
  Internet.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Group/individual.
INTRODUCTION
Identify the music from varied cultures to be played for appreciation.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Guide learners to listen to the music identified.
 Step 2: Learners to respond and react to the music freely with it before discussion.
 Step 3: Guide learners into a discussion about the music listened to, relating to appropriate events such
 as joyful celebrations.
 Step 4: Learners to appreciate the music they have listened to.
 SUMMARY:
 Review the lesson and note the summary points.
 CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to ask and answer questions related to the lesson.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Assign individual learners a project to be done out of school where they listen to music played on
television, radio or over the internet with the help of the parents.
